_note: Money is Thuso Money: payments, payouts, wallets, vouchers, gifts, group wallets, claims and Market orders. Every write is idempotent with a key. MyThuso never holds a card number. Wave 2 contract; Waves 3 and 5 build.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never holds a card number.
refusals.why: The provider's page takes it.

refusals.statement: A payout line does not name its own amount for a visit.
refusals.why: The share is packages/catalog/earnings.json's arithmetic.

refusals.statement: A suspension never touches money already earned.
refusals.why: Money does not subscribe to a suspension.

refusals.statement: A scheme receives nothing about a person's grant.
refusals.why: Money serves only the scheme's aggregate role.

refusals.statement: Nothing is charged without an idempotency key.
refusals.why: A retry is not a second charge. The binder asks for the key before either payment route's handler runs, and the ledger asks again, so both routes are named in case it is ever reached.

refusals.statement: Money does not hear that event.
refusals.why: Money hears the billable state changes packages/catalog/events.json lists under moneyHears, and an event carrying a reference into the record is refused even when its type is on the list.

refusals.statement: No doctor's payout is scheduled while the fee is undecided.
refusals.why: The documents give a range for a doctor's per-case fee, not a price. packages/catalog/money.json holds the fee as null until somebody named decides it, and a payout worked out from a number nobody decided is a promise nobody made.

refusals.statement: No scheme or employer sees what one person paid.
refusals.why: A scheme and an employer are served in aggregate. A person's payment tells whoever reads it that a visit happened, and when.

refusals.statement: That door is locked until its switch-on conditions are evidenced.
refusals.why: Payment results and payout advice arrive only through the doors in packages/catalog/feeds.json, and none of their conditions is met. In development the simulated provider stands behind them, in process, and nothing from the network does.

refusals.statement: This cash payment has had too many wrong codes and is held for the operations desk.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/money.json's attemptLimit. A six-digit code that can be tried without limit is a code that can be walked; after the limit even the right code is refused until the desk releases the payment.

refusals.statement: Cash is recorded against a finished visit, and this one has not finished.
refusals.why: A cash code entered before Care says the visit was billable would record money for a visit that may still not happen.

refusals.statement: This visit has no price Money can read yet, so nothing is charged.
refusals.why: appointment.booked@2 names the service, so the payable it opens is priced from packages/catalog/services.json as it opens. A payable can still have no price: one a store opened under appointment.booked@1, which named no service and is withdrawn, stays unpriced until visit.billable@1 names one. A charge against a payable with no catalogue price is an amount that came from the caller.

refusals.statement: A payout does not go down without a line naming the visit and the reason.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/earnings.json's every-deduction-is-named rule, enforced on the ledger rather than only drawn on the screen.

keptOnRefusal.why: A wrong code is refused, and the refusal rolls back everything else the handler did. The count of wrong codes and the audit row saying who entered one and when must survive that refusal, or the attempt limit never bites and a code can be walked by trying.

withdrawn.why: Built on the runtime, it had no true answer for two things a nurse can send. A reference to no cash payment could only be refused as a wrong code, which would count an attempt against nothing, or as a visit not finished, which is false. A nurse who does not hold the visit could only be told her role may not call the route, and a nurse's role may. Version two adds payable-not-found and cash-code-not-your-visit and keeps everything else. Its callers are version two's.

keptOnRefusal.why: A wrong code is refused, and the refusal rolls back everything else the handler did. The count of wrong codes and the audit row saying who entered one and when must survive that refusal, or the attempt limit never bites and a code can be walked by trying.

secretRequestFields.why: The patient's cash code. The runtime keeps a digest of every accepted request's fields to refuse a reused key; a digest of six digits would be the six digits to anybody holding the store file, so the code is left out of it.

routes.summary: The operations desk releases a cash payment held for too many wrong codes, after speaking to the patient.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The held cash payment, Money's own.

response.why: The payment's state, unchanged: releasing a hold pays nothing.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: Only a cash payment with a code can be held or released.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A release lets the nurse try again; the payment is published when the right code is entered.

withdrawn.why: It released a hold with no reason and had no field to carry one, so the audit of a release could say who and when and never why — and a hold lifted for no recorded reason is a code that can be walked five attempts at a time. Nor could it refuse releasing a payment that was not held. Version two takes a reason code from packages/catalog/money.json and refuses a release without one, with one the desk is not given, and of a payment that is not held. Its callers are version two's.

routes.summary: The operations desk releases a cash payment held for too many wrong codes, after speaking to the patient, with the reason written down.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same release once, and the audit gains one row.
The held cash payment, Money's own.

Why the hold is released, as one of packages/catalog/money.json's cash.releaseReasons: a code rather than free text, because the audit is read by finance and a desk's own words about a patient are where health information goes. Asked for by the handler rather than the binder, so that a release without one is refused in its own sentence.

response.why: The payment's state, unchanged: releasing a hold pays nothing.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: Only a cash payment with a code can be held or released.

refusals.statement: A held cash payment is released with a reason, or it is not released.
refusals.why: A hold is what stops a six-digit code being walked. Lifting it for no recorded reason gives whoever is trying another five attempts, and nobody reading the audit afterwards can tell a desk that spoke to the patient from one that pressed a button.

refusals.statement: That is not one of the reasons a held cash payment is released for.
refusals.why: The reasons are packages/catalog/money.json's. A reason nobody declared is a word nothing reads, and the audit is only useful if every row means something somebody agreed.

refusals.statement: This cash payment is not held, so there is nothing to release.
refusals.why: A release resets the wrong-code count. On a payment that is not held that would be a quiet way to hand a nurse, or whoever holds her phone, a fresh set of attempts.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A release lets the nurse try again; the payment is published when the right code is entered. No engine acts on a hold being lifted, and the event contract refuses an event nobody reads.

It was never built. Version two issues a voucher towards a visit or a plan at the catalogue's price, and POST /v1/money/voucher-redemptions@1 redeems it against a payable. withdrawn.why: It created a group wallet, and a wallet MyThuso keeps for a group is a deposit MyThuso holds for other people, which only a bank may take (packages/catalog/groups.json noPooledMoney). It named every member in the request that opened the group, so a member was added by whoever typed her token rather than by her own agreement, and it answered no refusal for a group paying for somebody who is not a member or an employer reading about an employee. It was never built. Version two opens a group that holds nothing; POST /v1/money/group-memberships@1 invites, a member agrees through .../accept@1, and POST /v1/money/group-payments@1 charges the group's own account for one member's payable. Its callers are those routes'.

refusals.statement: Only the role a setting names changes it, and the change is recorded against a named person.
refusals.why: A setting decides how the platform treats people. The role or capability the setting names changes it, and a change is recorded against somebody who can be asked about it; everybody else only reads what is in force.

refusals.statement: There is no setting by that name.
refusals.why: An unknown setting is refused rather than stored, or the history fills with changes nothing reads.

refusals.statement: A change to a setting says why, or it is not made.
refusals.why: The history is read after something has gone wrong. A change with no reason is a number somebody moved.

refusals.statement: These settings changed after you opened them. Read what is in force now and decide against that.
refusals.why: Two admins changing one setting from screens opened at the same time would each overwrite a decision they never saw.

refusals.statement: That is not the kind of value this setting holds.
refusals.why: A word where a number belongs, or a list where one choice belongs, is a guess at what the admin meant, and a setting is never set by a guess.

refusals.statement: This setting is never nought or less, whatever its range says.
refusals.why: A wait of nothing, an offer that lapses as it is made and a fee of nothing are never what anybody meant. The range is a proposal and could be set wrongly; this refusal does not depend on it.

refusals.statement: Every role a setting names is a role on the vetting register.
refusals.why: A role the register does not hold is a gate nobody can be vetted through, which looks like a shortage rather than a mistake.

refusals.statement: That wording is longer than this setting allows.
refusals.why: The maximum is the space the words are read in. Wording that does not fit is cut off where somebody reads it.

refusals.statement: That wording drops a sentence this setting must always keep.
refusals.why: Some wording carries a promise that protects somebody. It may be reworded around that sentence and never without it.

refusals.statement: That rota leaves hours uncovered that must always have somebody on them.
refusals.why: A rota with a gap is an alert with nobody to go to, and nobody finds out until one arrives.

refusals.statement: That is outside what an admin may set for this setting.
refusals.why: The bounds, the allowed values and the allowed roles sit beside the default in the engine's contract. Moving a setting past them is a change to that contract, not a setting.

refusals.statement: That is already the value in force, so there is nothing to change.

refusals.statement: A plan's name never sounds like medical aid, a scheme, cover or insurance.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/mom-plans.json refuses a plan being read as medical aid, and a name is read before any sentence. Asked from packages/catalog/money.json's wordingRules, after the shared rules.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: No engine acts on a settings change. The engine that owns a setting reads the value in force when it starts something, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to. A change is the row it appends to the engine's own history, which the read route returns.

routes.summary: Issue a voucher towards a visit or a MyThuso for Mom plan, at the catalogue's price, with its code shown once to whoever issued it.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same voucher once, and its code is not shown a second time.
service or plan, from packages/catalog/vouchers.json towards. Anything tied to a medicine, or to cash, a wallet, a bank or airtime, is refused in its own sentence.
For a voucher towards a visit: the service in packages/catalog/services.json whose price it is issued at.
For a voucher towards a plan: the MyThuso for Mom tier in packages/catalog/mom-plans.json whose monthly price it is issued at.

response.why: The code whoever holds the voucher redeems it with. In the first answer only, to whoever issued it; Money keeps a salted digest of it.
What the voucher holds, in cents: the catalogue's price for what it is towards on the day it was issued.
The last day it may be redeemed, from Money's setting voucher-expiry-years in force when it was issued, never sooner than section 63 of the Consumer Protection Act allows.

refusals.statement: A voucher is never tied to a medicine: not to buying one, collecting one or taking one.
refusals.why: Section 18A of the Medicines and Related Substances Act prohibits supplying a medicine under an incentive scheme, and the founder refuses any reward for taking a medicine pending counsel. packages/catalog/vouchers.json neverTowards names what is refused, by what a voucher is towards and by the fields a request sends.

refusals.statement: A voucher pays for care from the catalogue. It is never cash, and it is never paid out.
refusals.why: A voucher that becomes cash moves money nobody is billing for, and makes MyThuso a holder of prepaid balances. packages/catalog/vouchers.json cashOut.

refusals.statement: A voucher is issued only towards a visit or a plan the catalogue sells, at its price.
refusals.why: Its amount is the catalogue's price for what it is towards. A service nobody sells, a service no nurse can be sent for yet, or a tier with no price has no amount that did not come from the caller.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: An unredeemed voucher is money held against care not yet bought. No engine acts on one being issued, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to.

capabilityNamed.what: Vouchers in retail and spaza channels

secretResponseFields.shownOnce: The voucher's code was shown once, when it was issued, and is not shown again. Money keeps only a salted digest of it.

What stays on the voucher until it expires. It is never paid out.

The voucher's own expiry, as it was issued.

refusals.statement: That is more than is owed.
refusals.why: What a voucher paid past what is owed would be change, and change from a voucher is cash.

refusals.statement: A voucher pays for care from the catalogue. It is never cash, and it is never paid out.
refusals.why: A redemption is towards a payable and nothing else. A request carrying a cash, payout, bank, airtime, refund or transfer field is refused rather than ignored (packages/catalog/vouchers.json cashOut).

refusals.statement: That voucher is towards something else, so it cannot pay for this.
refusals.why: A voucher towards a visit pays for visits and one towards a plan pays for plans (packages/catalog/vouchers.json towards).

refusals.statement: That voucher has been used.
refusals.why: Nothing is left on it.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: A voucher pays towards Money's own payable, whose amount comes from the catalogue.

refusals.statement: That is not yours to pay.
refusals.why: A payable belongs to the person it was opened for and those named to pay it. Holding a voucher does not make somebody else's bill yours.

refusals.statement: A voucher is never tied to a medicine: not to buying one, collecting one or taking one.
refusals.why: A request that names a medicine, a prescription, a collection or a dose is refused, whatever the voucher is towards (packages/catalog/vouchers.json neverTowards).

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A redemption lowers what one payable owes inside Money. What is still owed is paid through POST /v1/money/payments@2, which publishes the payment, and no other engine acts on which part of a payable a voucher paid.

secretRequestFields.why: A voucher's code is a bearer credential: whoever holds it spends it. The runtime keeps a digest of every accepted request's fields to refuse a reused key, and the code is left out of it.

routes.summary: Ask for MyThuso for Mom for somebody: a son or daughter for a parent, or a person for herself. Nothing is owed and nothing starts until the person it is for agrees.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same request once.
Who the plan is for, as identity's opaque token. A patient asks only for herself.
The tier in packages/catalog/mom-plans.json. Only the one packages/catalog/mom-essential.json names may be asked for in this preview.

response.why: The plan asked for, Money's own.
The tier's monthly price from packages/catalog/mom-plans.json, in cents, so whoever asked sees what the first month would be before anything is owed.

refusals.statement: Only the monthly tier can be asked for in this preview. The others name devices, carers and reviews that do not exist yet.
refusals.why: Plus and Premium name a Thuso Band, a Thuso Home station, carers and a doctor's review of every visit, none of which exists (packages/catalog/capabilities.json). A plan sold for a promise nobody can keep is refused rather than billed.

refusals.statement: This person already has this plan, or one waiting for her to agree.
refusals.why: Two plans for one parent are one family billed twice for the same visits.

refusals.statement: No plan buys a place ahead of somebody else. When two people need a nurse urgently, the one who is more unwell is seen first, whatever either of them pays.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/mom-plans.json's refusal, word for word. A request asking for priority, a rank or a place in a queue is refused rather than ignored, because the founder has not decided what priority SOS means and no plan may put anybody ahead of somebody more unwell.

refusals.statement: A sponsor pays and never agrees for the parent. She agrees in her own account, or the plan does not start.
refusals.why: A request carrying an agreement, a consent or a signature on the parent's behalf is refused rather than recorded. No authority to act for another adult is proven (docs/governance/INFORMATION-OFFICER.md D-10).

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Money is the only engine that acts on a plan: it bills it, and it counts the visit and the collection the tier includes when it hears appointment.booked@2 and delivery.handed_over@1. No other engine acts on a plan being asked for, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to.

routes.summary: The person a plan is for agrees to it, as herself, and says how a line on her sponsor's statement reads.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same agreement once.
The plan asked for.
amount-only or service-named, from packages/catalog/programmes.json sponsor.lineDetail: whether a line on the sponsor's statement names the service. Hers to choose.

response.why: awaiting-payment, or active when a voucher already covered the first month.
The first month, Money's own payable, which the sponsor pays through POST /v1/money/payments@2 or a voucher towards the plan.

refusals.statement: Only the person a plan is for agrees to it, from her own account. A sponsor pays and never agrees for her.
refusals.why: A sponsor is a caller of this route so that the refusal is said in these words rather than as a role the route does not take: paying is what a sponsor may do, and agreeing is not. A patient who is not the person the plan is for is refused the same way. No guardian authority is proven (docs/governance/INFORMATION-OFFICER.md D-10), so a guardian is not a caller.

refusals.statement: There is no plan of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: The answer never says whether a plan exists for somebody else.

refusals.statement: Choose one of the ways a line on the statement may read.
refusals.why: The choices are packages/catalog/programmes.json's sponsor.lineDetail.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: An agreement opens the first month's payable in Money's own ledger. The payment publishes payment.succeeded@1, and no other engine acts on the agreement itself.

routes.summary: Read a plan as the person reading it may see it: its state and month, what it includes and has used, and what has happened on it, with what kind of care and which service only where the parent chose that. Never why, and never what was found.

request.why: The plan.

response.why: The tier's monthly price, from the catalogue.
The first month's payable, once she has agreed. Absent before, because nothing is owed until she does.
The day the first month was paid, which starts the plan. Absent before it started.
The last day of the plan month. Absent before it started.
What she chose a sponsor's line to say. Absent before she agreed.
Each inclusion Money counts, how many a month brings and how many this month has used.

fields.why: An inclusion id from packages/catalog/mom-plans.json's tier.
How many a plan month brings, from packages/catalog/mom-essential.json.
How many this plan month has used.

response.why: What has happened on the plan, oldest first: the day, and — for the parent, or for a sponsor when she chose service-named — what kind of care it was and which service. Never why, and never what was found.

fields.why: The day it happened.
visit or collection, or null for a sponsor while she has chosen amount-only.
The service in packages/catalog/services.json for a visit, or null for a collection and for a sponsor while she has chosen amount-only.

refusals.statement: There is no plan of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: Only the person the plan is for and the sponsor who asked for it read it, and the answer never says whether it exists for anybody else.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Reading changes nothing.

routes.summary: Open a group that pays for its members' care: a stokvel or a church, opened by a sponsor, or an employer. The group holds no money at MyThuso.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same group once.
stokvel, church or employer, from packages/catalog/groups.json kinds. Each kind names the role that opens it.

response.why: The group, Money's own. It is a reference and a kind, and nothing in it holds an amount.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never holds a group's money. A group pays for its members' care from its own account, one payment at a time, and nothing is pooled, deposited or kept here.
refusals.why: Holding money for other people is taking deposits, which only a bank may do (packages/catalog/groups.json noPooledMoney). A request carrying a balance, a deposit, a pool, a wallet or a contribution is refused rather than ignored, because an ignored field is a field somebody believes worked.

refusals.statement: A group is a stokvel, a church or an employer.
refusals.why: The kinds are packages/catalog/groups.json's, and each says who opens it and what a member may let it see.

refusals.statement: Only an employer opens a group for its staff, and only a person opens a stokvel or a church group.
refusals.why: An employer's group offers its members only the month's total, because an employer sees nothing about an employee's health. A stokvel opened by an employer would offer amounts and days to the one payer who must never see them.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A group is an arrangement between people, and nothing is owed or paid by opening one. No other engine acts on a group existing, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to.

routes.summary: A group invites somebody to let it pay for her care. Nothing is paid for her unless she agrees in her own account.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same invitation once.
The group inviting, which the caller opened.
Who is invited, as identity's opaque token.

response.why: The invitation, Money's own, which the person invited agrees to or does not.

refusals.statement: There is no group of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: Only the person who opened a group administers it, and the answer never says whether a group exists for somebody else.

refusals.statement: Nobody is made a member of a group without agreeing, in her own account. An invitation is all a group can send.
refusals.why: A request carrying an agreement, a consent or an acceptance for the person invited is refused rather than recorded (packages/catalog/groups.json memberFieldWords).

refusals.statement: MyThuso never holds a group's money. A group pays for its members' care from its own account, one payment at a time, and nothing is pooled, deposited or kept here.
refusals.why: An invitation carrying a contribution or a deposit is the pool the contract refuses, asked for one member at a time.

refusals.statement: This group already has as many members as a group may have.
refusals.why: Money's setting group-member-cap in force, counting everybody invited or agreed and nobody who left.

refusals.statement: This person has already been invited to this group, or is already a member.
refusals.why: Two invitations to one person are two answers she could give, and the group could read the one it preferred.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: An invitation changes nothing anybody owes. The person invited is asked when she opens her own account, and no other engine acts on an invitation.

routes.summary: The person invited agrees to let the group pay for her care, as herself, and chooses how the group's screen reads what it paid for her.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same agreement once.
The invitation.
amount-and-day or month-total-only, from packages/catalog/groups.json lineDetails, and only one her group's kind offers. Hers to choose.

refusals.statement: There is no invitation of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: Only the person invited and the person who invited her can name it, and the answer never says whether it exists for anybody else. An invitation she left is not open to agree to again; the group invites her afresh.

refusals.statement: Only the person invited agrees to join a group, from her own account. A group invites and never agrees for anybody.
refusals.why: A sponsor and an employer are callers of this route so that the refusal is said in these words rather than as a role the route does not take: inviting is what a group may do, and agreeing is not.

refusals.statement: An employer sees nothing about an employee's health: not who used care, not when and not what for.
refusals.why: An employee cannot choose to show her employer the day a visit was paid for, because the day is her health, and a choice made under an employer's eye is not freely made (packages/catalog/groups.json employer).

refusals.statement: Choose one of the ways this group may see what it paid for you.
refusals.why: The ways are packages/catalog/groups.json's, and each kind offers its own.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: An agreement lets the group pay for what she asks it to pay for later. A payment publishes payment.succeeded@1, and no other engine acts on the agreement itself.

routes.summary: A member leaves a group, as herself. It pays for nothing new, and what it already paid stays paid.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same leaving once.
Her membership.

refusals.statement: There is no invitation of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: A member leaves only her own membership.

refusals.statement: You are not a member of this group, so there is nothing to leave.
refusals.why: An invitation she never agreed to lets the group pay for nothing already; leaving it would record an agreement that was never given.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Leaving stops the group paying for what she asks after it. Nothing already paid is reversed, and no other engine acts on a membership ending.

routes.summary: A member asks her group to pay for a visit she owes: the group's own account is charged through the provider, up to the limit in force, and nothing is held at MyThuso.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same charge once.
The group she agreed to let pay for her.
What she owes, Money's own payable, for a visit.
card or eft, from packages/catalog/groups.json pays, on the provider's own page for the group's account.
What the payable owes, in cents: the catalogue's price for the service, less anything a voucher paid.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never takes a card number; the provider's page does.
refusals.why: Refused before it is logged, whoever's card it is.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never holds a group's money. A group pays for its members' care from its own account, one payment at a time, and nothing is pooled, deposited or kept here.
refusals.why: A charge asking to draw on a balance, a pool or a wallet names money that does not exist here and must not.

refusals.statement: A group pays only for its own members, and only for somebody who agreed to join it.
refusals.why: Somebody invited and not yet agreed, somebody who left, and somebody never invited are all refused in these words, so a group's account is never charged on anybody's word but a member's.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: A group pays towards Money's own payable, whose amount comes from the catalogue. One with no catalogue price yet has nothing Money can read as owed.

refusals.statement: That is not yours to pay.
refusals.why: A member asks her group to pay for her own visits and nobody else's.

refusals.statement: That way of paying is not offered for this.
refusals.why: A group pays for a visit by card or EFT (packages/catalog/groups.json pays): not cash, which is the patient's at her door, not a debit order and not a wallet.

refusals.statement: This has already been paid. Nothing was charged again.
refusals.why: A payable paid, or waiting on a cash code, is not paid a second time from a group's account.

refusals.statement: That amount is not what is owed.
refusals.why: A payable's amount comes from the catalogue.

refusals.statement: This would take what the group pays for you this month past its limit, so the group was not charged.
refusals.why: Money's setting group-member-monthly-limit-cents in force when she asks, counting what the group already paid for her this calendar month and any payment still waiting on the provider.

capabilityNamed.what: Group wallets for stokvels, churches and employers

routes.summary: Read a group as the person who opened it may see it: who agreed and what was paid, the day and the amount only where a member chose that, and for an employer only a month's total above the floor. Never what anybody's care was.

request.why: The group.

response.why: How many agreed. Left out for an employer while fewer agreed than packages/catalog/programmes.json's floor.
How many are invited and have not agreed. Left out for an employer below the floor.
What the group paid this calendar month for everybody together. Left out for an employer below the floor.
Each member's invitation and what she let the group see. Empty for an employer, always.

fields.why: The invitation.
invited, member or left.
What she chose, or null before she agreed.
The group's payments for her, only where she chose amount-and-day: the day and the amount, never the service or why.
The day the group was charged.
What it was charged.

refusals.statement: There is no group of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: Only the person who opened a group reads it.

refusals.statement: An employer sees nothing about an employee's health: not who used care, not when and not what for.
refusals.why: An employer asking for anything beyond its group is refused rather than answered with less, so the refusal is said and not guessed at.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Reading changes nothing.

routes.summary: Read your own invitations and memberships: which kind of group, whether you agreed and how, and what the group paid for you this month against its limit.

fields.why: The invitation.
stokvel, church or employer.
invited, member or left.
What you chose, or null before you agreed.
What the group was charged for you this calendar month.
Money's setting group-member-monthly-limit-cents in force now.

refusals.statement: You read only your own invitations and memberships.
refusals.why: A request naming anybody else, or asking for more than its own, is refused rather than answered with less.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Reading changes nothing.

routes.summary: The doctor who signed a visit's review drafts a claim to the patient's scheme for it: the billing half only, with no code and no amount of the caller's.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same draft once.
The visit's payable, Money's own, paid or still owed. The review is found from what Money heard, never named here.

response.why: Whether any code set is adopted: false in this build, so the draft says there is no code to choose.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: A claim is for Money's own payable for a visit, whose amount comes from the catalogue.

refusals.statement: A claim is drafted only for a visit that happened, whether it is paid or still owed.
refusals.why: Money learns a visit happened from visit.billable@1 and nowhere else. A cancelled visit, or one Care has not said was billable, is not care anybody can claim for.

refusals.statement: A claim is drafted only for a visit a doctor has signed a review of.
refusals.why: Money hears a signed review on review.billable@1 (packages/catalog/claims.json builtFrom). With no signed review about the same person, on or after the visit, there is nothing reviewed to claim for.

refusals.statement: Only the doctor who signed the review drafts its claim.
refusals.why: The doctor who signed is the one who answers for what the claim says was done.

refusals.statement: No code set is adopted in this build, so a claim carries no code: none is typed, none is chosen from a list and none is worked out from the service.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/claims.json codeSets. A request carrying a field named for a code or a coding is refused in these words rather than ignored.

refusals.statement: Money never receives why a service was needed.
refusals.why: Finance sees a service and an amount. A diagnosis is chosen inside the record and goes to the switching partner from there.

refusals.statement: This visit already has a claim. Nothing was drafted again.
refusals.why: One visit, one claim. A second draft under a new key is a scheme asked twice for one visit.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A draft is a record inside Money that the patient is asked about. No other engine acts on a claim being drafted, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to.

routes.summary: The patient agrees, as herself, to send a drafted claim to her scheme. It is not a grant to read her record, and the scheme is told nothing about her grants.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same agreement once.
The claim.

response.why: The last day the claim may be sent under this agreement: Money's setting claim-consent-days in force today, never longer than packages/catalog/consent.json's ceiling.

refusals.statement: There is no claim of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: Only the patient a claim is about agrees to it, and the answer never says whether a claim exists for anybody else.

refusals.statement: A scheme is told nothing about who else may read your record, and a claim carries none of it.
refusals.why: A scheme receives aggregate data only (packages/catalog/consent.json scheme-receives-aggregate-only). A request carrying a grant, a recipient, a scope or a sealed flag is refused rather than recorded.

refusals.statement: You have already agreed to send this claim. Nothing changed.
refusals.why: An agreement given again under a new key would move the day it runs out, which is a change she did not ask for.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: An agreement lets the claim be sent. Nothing is sent while no switching partner is connected, and no other engine acts on the agreement itself.

routes.summary: Ask for an agreed claim to be sent to the scheme. In this build every one stops: no switching partner is connected, and no code set is adopted.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same request once.
The claim.

response.why: submitted, the day a switching partner is connected. No answer of this version carries it in this build.

refusals.statement: There is no claim of yours with that reference.
refusals.why: A doctor sends only a claim she drafted; the back office any claim.

refusals.statement: A claim is sent only with the patient's agreement to send it, and this one does not have it.
refusals.why: A claim tells a scheme a person was seen, when and for what (packages/catalog/claims.json consent).

refusals.statement: The patient's agreement to send this claim has run out. Nothing was sent.
refusals.why: An agreement lasts the days in force when she gave it, and a claim sent after is sent on an agreement that no longer stands.

refusals.statement: Not submitted: no switching partner is connected.
refusals.why: A claim is sent only through the switching partner behind the claim-response door in packages/catalog/feeds.json, whose switch-on conditions are none of them met. The claim stays agreed and unsent.

refusals.statement: A claim is sent only with a code a clinician chose from an adopted code set, and no code set is adopted in this build.
refusals.why: Asked after the switching partner, because a code set is adopted with the partner (packages/catalog/claims.json gatesNote).

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Nothing is submitted while no switching partner is connected. claim.submitted@2 is the event for a claim that reached a scheme, and this version cannot publish it; the day a partner is connected is a new version of this route.

routes.summary: Read claims: the patient her own, and a doctor the ones she drafted, each with its state and why it has not been sent.

drafted or consented, the two states this build reaches.

refusals.statement: You read only the claims about you, or the ones you drafted.
refusals.why: A request naming anybody else, or asking for more than its own, is refused rather than answered with less.

routes.summary: The operations desk reads the cash payments held for too many wrong codes, to release each after speaking to the patient.

fields.why: The held payment, which POST /v1/money/payments/{paymentRef}/release@2 releases.
How many wrong codes it has had.
When the attempt limit held it, from the cash audit.

refusals.why: The desk speaks to the patient through the visit, not through this list. A request asking for a subject, a code or anything else is refused rather than answered with less.
